fact: The National Information and Communications Technology Policy 2016, signed by the Minister for Works, Transport and Communication in May 2016, is presented as the Government's revision of the 2003 policy and its framework for the ICT industry.

The full policy text, with preface, contents and chapters, is published as a PDF on the Ministry's official website (mawasiliano.go.tz); the document gives no date of posting, so its May 2016 publication date is used.

The Citizen reports the ICT Commission director general describing a 2016 policy, following the 2003 one, that put greater emphasis on digital systems and platforms; the document gives no adoption date beyond the year in the policy's name.
The Citizen reports that in 2021 the government launched a review process of the National ICT Policy (2016); no outcome is stated.

fact: The Minister for Works, Transport and Communication's foreword of December 2016 presents the National ICT Policy 2016 as formulated by the Government, replacing the 2003 policy, and the document is its five-year implementation strategy.

The strategy estimates Tsh. 248.2 billion is required over 2016/17 to 2020/21, financed from Government budget, development partners and the private sector, with a logframe of 22 objectives giving targets, indicators, resources per strategy, time frames and responsible institutions.

Each logframe strategy names responsible institutions, and the Ministry of Works, Transport and Communication issues the strategy, with the sector regulator TCRA assigned enforcement of laws and regulations.
The document names Government budget among three financing sources without tying a budget line to the policy, and lists adequate and timely budget allocations as an assumption.
